demand_mapping.implementation: Every answer task here uses the story text for this skill.
The second help of each answer task is a short English sentence frame; an answer after help is recorded apart.
About 30 minutes from the task types; a challenge only replaces an activity.
Nothing is collected away from the screen; back here, the student reports.
Answers are simulated text; reading aloud uses a simulated recording and score, not real pronunciation.
Nothing is assumed beforehand; the first answer without help is the sample.

resources.text: Mia has a toy car. She wants a bridge for her car. She puts two books on the table. There is a space between the books. Mia puts a piece of paper on the books. The paper makes a bridge. She puts her car on the paper. The paper bends. The car falls.

resources.purpose: Reading model: read-aloud-2
resources.text: “Can I make a new bridge?” says Mia. She folds a new piece of paper. She puts it on the same books. She tries the same car again. This time, the car stays on the bridge. Mia smiles. She draws the two bridges for Dad. “This one holds my car,” she says.
